organizations.name: Bass Anglers Sportsman Society
organizations.description: Founded in 1968, B.A.S.S. runs the Bassmaster Elite Series, the Opens, and the sport's defining championship — the Bassmaster Classic.

organizations.name: Major League Fishing
organizations.description: Home of the catch-weigh-immediately-release format, the Bass Pro Tour, the Invitationals, the Toyota Series and the grassroots Phoenix Bass Fishing League.

organizations.name: National Professional Fishing League
organizations.description: An angler-first professional tour founded in 2021 on a flat entry fee, a capped field, and a published payout table.

series.name: Bassmaster Elite Series
series.description: The top rung at B.A.S.S. — roughly 100 of the best boaters in the world over an eight- or nine-event season, racing for Angler of the Year and a Classic berth.

series.name: Bassmaster Open Series
series.description: The qualifying path to the Elites. Fish one division or fish them all; the top finishers earn Elite invitations.

series.name: Bassmaster Classic
series.description: The world championship of bass fishing. Roughly 55 qualifiers, three days, one trophy.

series.name: B.A.S.S. Nation
series.description: The grassroots club circuit — state federations feeding regional championships and a shot at the Classic.

series.name: Bassmaster College Series
series.description: Two-angler university teams fishing for a national title and a Classic berth for the winner.

series.name: Bassmaster High School Series
series.description: Two-angler high school teams with a boat captain, fishing state and national events.

series.name: Bass Pro Tour
series.description: MLF's flagship: 80 anglers, no five-fish limit, every scorable bass counts on SCORETRACKER as it is caught.

series.name: Tackle Warehouse Invitationals
series.description: The direct qualifier to the Bass Pro Tour — traditional five-fish-limit events with a 150-angler field.

series.name: Toyota Series
series.description: Regional three-day events with a boater and co-angler division, feeding a year-end championship.

series.name: Phoenix Bass Fishing League
series.description: The entry point to tournament bass fishing — 24 regional divisions of one-day weekend events.

series.name: Abu Garcia College Fishing
series.description: Two-angler collegiate teams across four conferences and a national championship.

series.name: NPFL Tour
series.description: A capped 120-boat professional field, flat entry fees, and a payout table published before the season starts.

series.name: NPFL Championship
series.description: The season-ending shootout for the NPFL's top points earners.

articles.title: Avery Ingalls wins Nation on Lake Chatuge
articles.dek: 0.48 pounds separated first from second after 3 days on Lake Chatuge.
articles.bodyMd:
**Hiawassee, GA** — Avery Ingalls of Mountain Home, AR closed out the 2026 B.A.S.S. Nation stop on Lake Chatuge with 67.06 pounds, winning by 0.48 pounds and collecting $10,000.

## How it was won

Ingalls opened with 25.28 pounds on day one and never gave the lead back, finishing the 3-day event with 15 scorable fish. A five-fish limit each day meant culling was the whole game, and the right afternoon bites made the difference.

Dalton Thibodeaux finished second with 66.58 pounds, ahead of Kendall Ortega at 64.77 pounds.

## Big bass

The heaviest fish of the week went to Gage Shelby at 9.93 pounds.

## What it means

The win moves Ingalls up the 2026 Nation points race with 200 points banked from Lake Chatuge.
articles.author: bass-stats staff
